title: The Afternoon Brief: Makhachev seeks UFC record as Ohtani nears return; tragedy in Portugal
dek: Saturday's midday slate pivoted from recovery and record pursuit to tragedy and discipline: Islam Makhachev defends his welterweight title chasing a 17th consecutive victory, Ohtani's bullpen progress continues on schedule toward a seasonal return, and a cyclist's death in Portugal has prompted withdrawal and raised safety questions.
author: GoCheckMySports
key_fact: Makhachev's historic win streak attempt collides with undefeated Machado Garry in Philadelphia tonight, while Ohtani's controlled recovery and Scheffler's final-round push remain on track; separately, Finlay Tarling's death during the Volta a Portugal has withdrawn NSN's development squad and opened investigation into course safety protocols.
bottom_line: Makhachev pursues a historic UFC record tonight against an undefeated challenger; Scheffler chases his first win since January in Sunday's St. Jude final round; Ohtani's recovery stays on schedule toward a seasonal return within weeks; and van Rooyen's suspension removes a forward from Melbourne's finals push. In Portugal, Finlay Tarling's death has prompted NSN's withdrawal and raised unresolved questions about course safety procedures. Watch for the outcomes in Philadelphia and Southwind, Ohtani's next bullpen session within two to five days, any findings from authorities investigating the cycling incident, and whether Melbourne appeals van Rooyen's suspension.
body: The midday picture splits between sport proceeding as planned and sport interrupted by tragedy. Makhachev's welterweight title defense against Machado Garry at UFC 330 in Philadelphia on Saturday carries the weight of history: the 34-year-old Russian enters with a 16-fight win streak and the chance to set a new UFC consecutive-victory record at 17, one shy of Anderson Silva's mark. Machado Garry, undefeated, arrives seeking a signature victory that would derail the record pursuit. The pairing tests whether the pressure of chasing a historic streak alters Makhachev's tactical approach.

In golf, Scheffler enters the St. Jude final round at TPC Southwind with a two-shot lead at 13-under over Burns and Im. The reporting shows Scheffler, the world No. 1, chasing his first victory since January despite a season of strong positioning and runner-up finishes. Burns, tied for second at 11-under, will pair with Scheffler in Sunday's final group for the first time as contenders, a pairing with history: Burns defeated Scheffler in a playoff at Colonial in 2022. The final 18 holes will test whether Scheffler converts his lead into the close-out he has not achieved all season.

Ohtani's recovery remains on the accelerated timeline the Dodgers outlined Friday. His 35-pitch bullpen session marked his first mound work in more than three weeks since his July 3 left knee injury. Manager Dave Roberts expressed confidence Ohtani will throw another bullpen session within two to five days, after which the path to major league competition should clarify. The progression depends on no setback; the reporting does not indicate any complication to date.

In professional rugby, Australia defeated Japan 56-17 in Townsville to extend its win streak to three Tests, the first such run since 2024 under new coach Les Kiss. The Wallabies trailed at halftime before dominating the second half through set-piece and breakdown execution. The margin masks a tighter opening 40 minutes but establishes momentum heading into Nations Championship play.

In the NFL, Marcus Mariota suffered a sprained MCL during Friday's preseason opener against Miami and will miss the remainder of the preseason. The backup quarterback departed after four plays on a noncontact injury, walking off under his own power. Washington will proceed through the preseason with Jayden Daniels as the only immediately available starter at the position.

In Australian Rules Football, Jacob van Rooyen received a three-match suspension for a swinging arm strike that knocked out Port Adelaide's Aliir Aliir during Saturday night's match. The ban removes a key forward from Melbourne's roster heading into finals, extending through the Demons' first two playoff matches depending on ladder position. The incident occurred in the second term; Aliir was knocked unconscious and failed his Head Injury Assessment test.

In cycling, tragedy halted competition when Finlay Tarling, a 19-year-old Welsh time-trial specialist, died Friday during the Volta a Portugal. Local media reports cited by ESPN indicate a car entered the race road going in the opposite direction and struck Tarling after missing warning signs from race stewards. NSN withdrew its development squad from the event Saturday. The reporting does not indicate whether authorities have completed an initial investigation into the sequence of events or what findings may have emerged.
